content:
Written: Ben Fisher
Artist: Pedro Andreo
Rating: 4.5 out of 5


# **Summary**
Eydis Frigsdottir is a chain smoking Icelandic attorney and descendent of the goddess Frigg. Blessed with the gift of making unbreakable contracts, she is often wrangled into settling disputes between Mythological creatures and humans. Vali, one of the many sons of Odin, has come to her to have her be his mediator between himself and his half brother Hodr. Turns out that Hodr has an issue with the torture he endured after Vali was ‘forged’ and given the divine purpose of killing him. Eydis initially brushes this off, stating she only deals with Elves, Trolls, and the occasional Ogre, and ends up taking a waitress named Addy back to her house. The next day the antics of Hodr and his brother Balor leads to Addy becoming collateral damage and resolving Eydis to take the case

![image](https://image.nostr.build/484eb482872e724ce6301969e4aeba521b40ad227192696ce069015181e363ae.jpg)

# Review
Valhalaw is probably my favorite #1 issue that I read last month. I think the concept is not only extremely interesting but I think it has so much potential to go in so many different directions, keeping us in anticipation for the next issue. I love the establishment of Eydis as this jaded lawyer who could really care less about the responsibilities that have placed on her shoulders, but she’s got to pay the bills somehow. I think it places her in a great position to dive into her psyche and see what makes her tick and what motivates her. I highly recommend you pick this issue up where you can, I’m excited to keep up with it as it is realized and whenever I can get my hands on it. Let’s dive into some of my favorite moments from this issue: 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/a925f526cc85168c0e0b9885617f54a64766d9f864ad4e266e5f27c973e0ba27.jpg)

Right off the bat I know what type of comic I’m getting into and I think that is a really strong skill to have when it comes to story telling. We get a peak into the life Eydis on a day to day basis and it presents such unique life that we simply want to know more. In this scene she is wrapping up negotiations with an Elf and a farmer and let’s them know that they can move the rock, I’m assuming her dwelling, but they have to keep it facing north. The farmer is ecstatic by this as he is hoping to expand his farm. Eydis then tells him he can pay her in cash or in Vodka - if you want to cut out the middle man. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/73f60cea8ccb6fedb6e14a41784e9edfb7eb9bd5e122dfa7ed4504e3fcadd3f3.jpg)
![image](https://image.nostr.build/c4081125408290675f0160cf715554889ca630f7971e7292a67fcf13bf9a9958.jpg)

After Eydis has brushed off the Son of Odin for her law services, what a sentence that is, she heads back to her place to serve Addy in another way. When she wakes up to a toothy frog in a very cute hat waiting for her she realizes she is late for her mediation between her a fox like creature. The biggest surprise though is that Addy seems very unfazed by the fact that a fox and a frog just walked in asking her one night stand for legal advice. She even asks if she can tag along and maybe stick around for another night. We get a great line form Eydis after this “You know what? I like those terms. It’s a deal. But Words of Advice: You’ll want to be a lot more careful about making those with me in the future”. I think Eydis is really taken a back by this, and possibly not just cause she’s okay with her unique situation but that Addy wants to stick around for another night. I think Eydis keeps people at an arms length so she’s conditioned to people not wanting to spend time with her. This could be a nice turning point

![image](https://image.nostr.build/63fce0d391b41bdcab9a69a8596722103e9dd8380554f1eca0f0af37dfd9a320.jpg)
![image](https://image.nostr.build/329914b39eeea5caf693a8ab5eec94abb418a345470497aa16474291e5b1b416.jpg)

Unfortunately when you work close with the Gods, you aren’t immune to their antics and destruction. Hodr and his brother Balor are back on earth, looking for revenge, and doesn’t seem to care who gets in their way. A police chase leads to a flying police cruiser landing square in the center of where Addy was standing and her chances of survival seem pretty low. Eydis is in shock by this but brushes her jacket off, gathers her papers and then her courage, and walks past the police barricade to serve those mediation papers to Hodr himself. I think Eydis saw a slightly brighter future ahead when she connected with Addy, and for it to be snuffed out so quickly and right in front of her, she can direct that anger towards a Son of Odin. 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/a0325ec3dcebcc5fce267c95b02bad6057ba7695fb410bcc60e1e7c4bf193afe.jpg)

We do have a small ray of hope that Addy could be back. Just before the moment Eydis is asking her how she hasn’t run for the hills yet, Addy talks about her mother who told her the tales of these creatures and the Gods and she grew so accustomed to hearing them that she believes them. She then reveals she has a rune marked on the back of neck that apparently was just a bonding experience with her and her siblings, but could potentially be a protection rune. We will have to wait and see 

![image](https://image.nostr.build/1e9d841a6d848f8ef2cc2cc5ac291b23829f4cbc03aa5594664d27ac7581eecd.jpg)

Overall I’m excited to see where this story goes. The possibilities are pretty endless with a story like this and I’m enjoying this John Constantine type character. Thanks for reading and keep your eyes on the website for additional essays by me, covering #1 issues of comics I have read. Comics are an incredible medium that has really captured me for the past couple years and I am really excited to share my insights with yall and hopefully show off some great comics.
